DTG vs. DTF vs. screen printing

There is no single best method for every job. Quantity, artwork, garment fabric, deadline, and desired feel determine which process makes the most sense.

General comparison for custom apparel. Exact results and pricing vary by artwork, garment, placement, and production requirements.
FactorDTGDTFScreen printing
Minimum orderNo minimumNo minimumOften has a practical minimum because of setup
Setup feesUsually lowUsually lowCommonly charged by design and color
TurnaroundSame-day may be availableSame-day may be availableUsually requires more setup time
Colors and photo detailFull color, gradients, and fine photo detailFull color, bright whites, gradients, and fine detailExcellent spot colors; photo work needs more complex separations and setup
Estimated cost at 1 piece*About $25About $25Usually not economical for one shirt
Estimated cost at 12 pieces*About $18 eachAbout $18 eachSetup can keep the per-shirt price higher, especially with multiple colors
Estimated cost at 100 pieces*About $15 eachAbout $15 eachCan be the lowest-cost choice for a simple one- or two-color design
Feel on fabricSoft and breathable, especially on light cotton garmentsSmooth, slightly raised transfer feel; large solid areas feel less breathableVaries by ink and coverage, from soft water-based prints to a heavier ink layer
DurabilityGood when properly cured and cared forVery good when properly applied and cared forExcellent when properly printed and cured
Best fabric matchesCotton and cotton-rich blendsCotton, polyester, blends, and many heat-compatible itemsMany fabrics when the correct ink system is used

*Illustrative Image On estimates use the site's current pricing model for a standard $8 shirt with one large decoration: $25 at one piece, $18 each at 12, and $15 each at 100. Dark garments, extra placements, premium blanks, oversized artwork, special handling, taxes, and other project details can change the final quote. Image On does not quote or provide screen printing.

Digital apparel options

Choose the method that fits the artwork and garment

What is DTG?

Direct-to-garment printing applies textile ink directly to the shirt. It is especially effective for cotton and cotton-rich garments when you want a soft print with full color, shading, gradients, or photo-quality detail.

  • No minimum order
  • Soft feel on cotton
  • Strong choice for photographs and detailed art

What is DTF?

Direct-to-film printing creates the design on transfer film, then applies it with heat. It produces bright, durable artwork and works across more material types than a typical DTG project.

  • Cotton, polyester, and blends
  • Useful for shirts, compatible bags, and pressable hat styles
  • Full color with no minimum order

Which is better for my order?

Choose based on the shirt fabric, graphic, placement, quantity, and deadline. DTG often wins for a soft photo print on cotton; DTF often wins when you need fabric flexibility, bright opacity, or unusual placement options.

  • Send the artwork first
  • Choose garments after discussing the process
  • Confirm timing before placing a rush order
The honest answer

When screen printing makes more sense

Screen printing can be the better production method for a very large run using one or two solid ink colors. Once the screens are prepared, repeating the same simple design across hundreds of identical garments can bring the unit price down.

It can also be a strong fit when a project requires a particular specialty ink or a traditional printed finish. Image On does not provide that process, but we would rather explain the tradeoff clearly than recommend the wrong method for your order.

Frequently asked questions

DTG, DTF, and same-day shirt questions

Is DTG as good as screen printing?

Yes, for the right project. DTG is an excellent choice for cotton shirts, small or medium quantities, photo-quality artwork, gradients, and a soft feel. Screen printing may be more economical for very large runs with one or two simple colors.

Does DTF crack or peel?

A properly applied DTF transfer is designed to be durable, but incorrect application, excessive heat, harsh chemicals, and repeated high-temperature drying can shorten its life. Wash inside out in cool water and follow the shop's care instructions.

Can I get custom shirts same day in San Diego?

Same-day DTG or DTF service may be available through Image On's Santee and Downtown San Diego shops. Availability depends on artwork, garment stock, quantity, placement, and the current production schedule, so call the preferred location first.

What's the minimum order?

Image On does not require a minimum for DTG or DTF custom shirts. You can ask about one shirt, a dozen, or a larger group order. Pricing per shirt generally improves as quantity increases.
